title: Your first day on the team
instruction: Join a team building a new customer portal. Explain your work and ask for the help you need

vocabulary.example: My first task is to build the login screen
vocabulary.exampleTranslation: Minha primeira tarefa é criar a tela de login

vocabulary.example: I need access to the repository

vocabulary.exampleTranslation: A falta de acesso é um impedimento

call.text: Hi, welcome to the team! I’m Kim. Can you hear me clearly?
call.cue: Confirm that you can hear Kim
call.example: Yes, I can hear you clearly

call.text: Let’s start with a quick introduction. What’s your name, and what do you work with?
call.cue: Introduce yourself and what you work with
call.example: My name is Alex, and I’m a frontend developer

call.text: I work on the frontend. Which tools do you use most?
call.cue: Tell Kim which tools you use
call.hint: I mostly use… / I also use…
call.example: I mostly use React and TypeScript, and I also use Git every day

call.text: Today, your task is to build the login screen for our new customer portal. You’re working on the frontend. Could you repeat that back to me?
call.cue: Confirm which screen you will build and which part of the project you will work on
call.hint: So, I’ll build… / I’ll work on…
call.example: So, I’ll build the Login screen and work on the frontend of the customer portal

call.text: I’ll send you the setup guide after this call. Can you message me if you need access?
call.cue: Confirm that you will message her if you need access
call.example: Sure, I’ll message you if I need access to the project

feedback.text: Thanks for showing the login screen. The form is clear, and the error message helps. Could you make the Forgot password link easier to find on mobile? Let’s add that to our next tasks.

shadowing.text: Could you give me access to the repository?
What should happen when the user clicks Sign in?
I’m blocked because I don’t have access yet
The deadline is Friday. Is that still correct?
Thanks for the feedback. I’ll update the task

daily.question: How is the Login screen going?
daily.cue: Use the board to explain what is ready and what is still missing
daily.hint: The layout is… / I still need…
daily.example: The Login layout is ready, but I’m still waiting for the test API address

daily.question: What is stopping you from connecting it to the backend?
daily.cue: Explain the blocker and ask for the help you need
daily.example: I’m waiting for the test API address — could you send it to me?

daily.question: Priya can send the test API address after lunch. What can you do while you wait?
daily.cue: Agree on useful work you can do before connecting the API
daily.hint: While I wait, I can… / Once I have it, I’ll…
daily.example: While I wait, I can test the layout and error message, and I’ll connect the API after lunch

planningCall.text: We’re building the customer portal. You own the login screen. What should a customer be able to do in the first version?
planningCall.cue: Explain what the Login screen needs to do
planningCall.hint: The customer can… / The first version needs…
planningCall.example: The customer can sign in with an email and password and reset their password if they forget it

planningCall.text: I’d add Google login first. Most people don’t want another password. Why start with email and password?
planningCall.cue: Discuss Owen’s suggestion and explain your choice for the first version
planningCall.hint: I see your point, but… / For Friday, I’d…
planningCall.example: I see your point, but I’d start with email and password to keep Friday’s version small

planningCall.text: The email and password API is ready. Google login would need more backend work. What information do you need from me?
planningCall.cue: Ask for the API information or support you need
planningCall.hint: Could you send me…? / What happens if…?
planningCall.example: Could you send me the API URL and the error response for an incorrect password?

planningCall.text: I’ve finished the password reset screen. Your login screen only needs a Forgot password link to open it. Where will you put that link?
planningCall.cue: Explain where the link should be and why
planningCall.hint: I’d put it… / That would help people…
planningCall.example: I’d put the Forgot password link below the password field so customers can find it easily

planningCall.text: What should the screen show if the email or password is wrong? We need to make that clear without losing what the customer typed.
planningCall.cue: Suggest how the Login screen should handle the error
planningCall.hint: I’d show… / I’d keep… / Should we…?
planningCall.example: I’d show a clear error message and keep the email so the customer can try again

planningCall.text: Let’s agree on this version before we finish. What will you deliver by Friday, and what will you leave for later?
planningCall.cue: Summarise the agreed first version and the next step
planningCall.hint: By Friday, I’ll… / We’ll leave… for later
planningCall.example: By Friday, I’ll deliver email and password login with error handling and a reset link, and we’ll leave Google login for later

reviewCall.text: I’ve finished the registration screen. A new customer can enter their name, email and password, then create an account. If an email is already in use, the page shows a clear message.

I’ve built the password reset screen. The customer enters their email and asks for a reset link. After they send it, the page tells them to check their inbox. They don’t need to remember their old password.

The backend now supports registration, login and password reset. The login API checks the email and password. If they are correct, it returns a session. If not, it returns an error for the screen to show.
Now show us your login screen. Explain how a customer signs in, what happens when the password is wrong, and how they can reset it.
reviewCall.cue: Present the Login screen: signing in, a wrong password and password recovery
reviewCall.hint: The customer enters… / If… / They can…
reviewCall.example: Customers sign in with an email and password, see an error if either is wrong, and use Forgot password to reset it

accessPractice.question: Can you open the customer-portal repository?
accessPractice.cue: Explain the error you can see and ask for access
accessPractice.hint: I can’t open… / It says… / Could you…?

accessPractice.question: Which work email should I give access to?
accessPractice.cue: Give the work email shown on the screen and confirm the repository
accessPractice.hint: Please use… / I need access to…

accessPractice.question: I’ve added you. What will you do next?
accessPractice.cue: Thank your teammate and explain your first step

independent.question: Can we show the Login screen in Friday’s demo?
independent.cue: Explain what is ready and what is blocking the test
independent.hint: The screen is… / The test account…

independent.question: What do you need from me to unblock it?
independent.cue: Ask your teammate for specific help
independent.hint: Could you…? / I need… so I can…

independent.question: I can activate a test account after lunch. What will you check next?
independent.cue: Agree on the next test and when you will give an update
independent.hint: Once it’s active, I’ll… / I’ll update you…
